papers.title: Biomechanically optimized 3D-Printed titanium prostheses with stiffener arrangement for critical femoral diaphyseal defects: early weight-bearing capacity and combat readiness validated through integrated biomechanical-FEA approach
papers.abstract: Introduction: Critical femoral diaphyseal defects exceeding 3 cm present significant challenges in trauma and military orthopedics, particularly in blast injury scenarios requiring rapid rehabilitation. Methods: performance of two personalized prostheses (Groups A and B) designed explicitly for critical femoral diaphyseal defects through integrated biomechanical testing and finite element analysis (FEA). Using fourth-generation composite femurs simulating 10 cm defects (n = 16), we compared axial compression, torsion, four-point bending stiffness, and cyclic fatigue performance against intact bones (Group D) and diaphyseal fractures without defects (Group C). Results: Key findings demonstrate comparable compressive stiffness between prostheses groups (Group A: 764.12±112.63 N/mm; Group B: 693.63±136.31 N/mm) and intact femurs (808.59±18.1 N/mm, p>0.05). The torsional stiffness is comparable between prostheses groups (Group A: 2.28±0.15 Nm/°; Group B: 2.18±0.22 Nm/°) versus diaphyseal fractures without defects (2.01±0.19 Nm/°). The stiffness results comply with mobilization requirements. FEA revealed maximum von Mises stresses in prosthesis fixation systems below the yield strength of Ti6Al4V, with digital image correlation validating the stress distribution patterns. The porous scaffold design achieved optimal modulus (1,132.85 MPa) between cortical and cancellous bone, reducing the "stress shielding" effect. Both prostheses endured 1800 N cyclic loading (100,000 cycles ≈, 13.3 years of physiological use) without structural failure. Discussion: These customized prostheses address critical military medical needs by enabling immediate weight-bearing, reducing surgical complexity compared to bone transport techniques, and maintaining long-term mechanical integrity. The stiffener design philosophy and additive manufacturing flexibility provide adaptable solutions for complex combat-related trauma, significantly advancing early functional recovery in resource-constrained environments.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文涉及钛合金3D打印股骨缺损假体的力学设计与验证，对股骨柄结构设计有方法学参考价值，但并非直接针对髋关节柄。
llm.why_not_core: The paper focuses on critical femoral diaphyseal defect reconstruction, not on femoral stem (hip stem) design for arthroplasty; no hip stem or acetabular interface is involved.

summary_zh.motivation: 针对股骨10 cm临界缺损，设计可早期承重的个性化钛合金假体。
summary_zh.method: 通过力学测试和有限元分析对比两种假体设计，评估刚度、疲劳及应力遮挡。
summary_zh.result: 假体刚度接近完整股骨，100,000次循环载荷无失效，多孔结构降低应力遮挡。
summary_zh.validation: 复合股骨模型力学测试与数字图像相关验证FEA应力分布。

summary_en.motivation: To design personalized Ti6Al4V prostheses for critical femoral diaphyseal defects that enable immediate weight-bearing and rapid rehabilitation.
summary_en.method: Integrated biomechanical testing (compression, torsion, bending, fatigue) and finite element analysis on composite femurs with 10 cm defects, comparing two stiffener designs.
summary_en.result: Both prostheses exhibited stiffness comparable to intact femurs, survived 1800 N cyclic loading for 100,000 cycles, and the porous scaffold reduced stress shielding.
summary_en.validation: In vitro mechanical tests on fourth-generation composite femurs and digital image correlation validated FEA stress distributions.
